related.text:
The Philippine peso continued its downtrend for the second straight trading day on Thursday.
The local currency shed 45 centavos to close at P63.7:$1, from P63.25:$1.
Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. chief economist Michael Ricafort attributed the peso’s weakness to “higher US dollar versus major global currencies.”
The dollar’s strength came “amid increased odds of future Fed rate hike/s in the coming months a day after faster-than-expected US CPI (consumer price index) data.”

article.text:
THE peso weakened further on Thursday, losing by 45 centavos against the greenback, while the main index of the Philippines Stock exchange fell as investors remained cautious amid corporate earnings releases.
The local currency closed at P63.7, weaker than the P63.25 posted on Wednesday. It opened at P63.25 and traded from P63.25 to P63.7.
The volume reached $1.720 trillion, up from the previous P1.421 trillion.
Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. chief economist Michael Ricafort said the peso weakened as the US dollar strengthened against major global currencies.
He added that this “increased the odds of future US Fed rate hike,” which could weigh on the local currency.
The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index (PSEi), meanwhile, closed lower amid the downward revision in the country’s economic growth outlook.
Although net foreign buying helped limit the decline.
The benchmark index slipped 0.57 percent, or 32.41 points, to close at 5,660.55. Despite the decline, foreign investors were net buyers, recording inflows of P329 million.
Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said investors remained cautious following BMI’s downward revision of its Philippine economic growth forecasts, which added to concerns about the country’s economic trajectory.
Market participants also stayed on the sidelines while awaiting further corporate earnings results and fresh catalysts that could support a recovery, he said.
Among actively traded stocks, Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) and PLDT Inc. declined ahead of their removal from MSCI indexes, while GCash-related shares gained amid foreign buying, according to AB Capital Securities Inc.
The information technology sector recorded the biggest value turnover at P2.15 billion, while financials and property stocks posted smaller declines.
Industrial stocks led sectoral losses, falling 1.78 percent, followed by mining and oil, which dropped 3.91 percent. Services declined 0.37 percent, while holdings shed 0.76 percent.
The broader market was negative, with 131 decliners against 41 advancers, while 62 issues were unchanged. Total value turnover reached P6.71 billion, excluding extraordinary block sales.
Among index constituents, SMC Corp. led gainers, rising 4.10 percent, followed by Globe Telecom Inc., which added 4.06 percent. Universal Robina Corp. and JG Summit Holdings Inc. also advanced.
ACEN Corp. was the biggest index decliner, falling 8.05 percent, followed by Semirara Mining and Power Corp., which lost 6.91 percent, and GT Capital Holdings Inc., which dropped 5.35 percent.
The peso also weakened, with the dollar trading at P63.68, up 0.68 percent.

reasons: reader relevance 3/3: Credit card finance charge cap kept at 3%

related.title: BSP keeps 3% cap on credit card finance charges

article.text:
THE Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has retained the existing cap on credit card finance charges but allowed banks and other credit card issuers to collect higher fees on installment loans and cash advances.
In a circular on Thursday, signed by BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr., the monthly add-on rate ceiling for credit card installment loans will increase to 1.5 percent from 1 percent, while the maximum one-time processing fee for cash advances will rise to P300 from P200 per transaction.
“Such maximum processing fee and interest rates or finance charges shall be subject to periodic review by the Bangko Sentral,” Remolona said.
In a separate statement, the central bank said these “adjustments aim to balance consumer protection with access to credit.”
“They also provide credit card issuers more flexibility in setting charges as operating costs rise,” it added.
Despite the changes, the BSP maintained the 3-percent monthly ceiling on finance charges for regular credit card transactions, equivalent to an annual interest rate of 36 percent.
The central bank first introduced the ceilings in 2020 as part of measures to protect credit card borrowers, with partial adjustments made in 2023. The latest revisions are covered by BSP Circular 1242, issued on Nov. 10.
It regularly reviews credit card fee and charge ceilings, taking into consideration prevailing economic conditions, the financial soundness of banks and other financial institutions, and consistency with its monetary policy settings, among other factors.
The revised ceilings will apply only to new transactions entered into from the circular’s effectivity date, which is 15 calendar days after its publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
Existing credit card installment loans will remain subject to their previously agreed terms and conditions, the central bank said.
“All credit card fees and charges remain subject to existing consumer protection, disclosure and transparency requirements,” it added.

deepDives.summary: Low-cost carrier Cebu Pacific has fallen into a wider net loss of almost P13 billion in nine months, as expenses rose quicker than revenue, pulled by higher jet fuel prices.
reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Airline loss from jet fuel costs may affect fares

related.title: High fuel prices, peso slump ground CebuPac to P12.8-B loss
Cebu Pacific reports P12.78B Jan-Sept. loss
related.text:
BUDGET carrier Cebu Pacific swung to a P12.78-billion net loss in the first nine months of the year from a P9.47-billion profit in the same period in 2025, as higher fuel costs and foreign exchange losses outweighed revenue gains.
In a disclosure on Thursday, the airline reported a third-quarter net loss of P6.91 billion, reversing a P499.02-million profit a year earlier.
Quarterly revenues rose to P27.66 billion from P24.27 billion.
For the nine-month period, consolidated revenues grew 9.8 percent to P96.22 billion. Higher passenger volume lifted passenger revenues by 9.5 percent to P65.31 billion, while cargo revenues expanded 12.6 percent to P5.84 billion and ancillary revenues increased 10.2 percent to P25.07 billion.
Operating expenses climbed 24.3 percent to P99.23 billion. The airline reported an operating loss of P3.3 billion, reversing a P7.79-billion operating profit a year earlier.
Fuel expenses jumped 62.4 percent to P39.1 billion, pushing flying operations expenses up 51.6 percent to P44.13 billion. The airline attributed the jump in jet fuel prices to disruptions following the Feb. 28 escalation of the war in the Middle East.
Foreign exchange losses quadrupled to P5.03 billion as the peso weakened against the US dollar, Japanese yen and Singapore dollar. Financing costs and other charges totaled P6.05 billion.
“The third quarter remained a challenging period, as elevated fuel prices, a weaker peso, and broader macroeconomic pressures continued to affect our operations,” Cebu Pacific CEO Michael Szucs said.
But he added that the airline was encouraged by a return to passenger growth. Cebu Pacific said bookings for the holiday season and Q1 of 2027 remained healthy, while improving yields bolstered its revenue outlook.
Looking ahead to 2027, the company said forward bookings for the holiday season and ongoing improvement in yields provides greater confidence in its revenue outlook for Q4 this year and beyond.

MANILA, Philippines — Low-cost carrier Cebu Pacific has fallen into a wider net loss of almost P13 billion in nine months, as expenses rose quicker than revenue, pulled by higher jet fuel prices.
Based on its financial report, Cebu Pacific’s parent Cebu Air Inc. said its net loss worsened to P12.84 billion in the nine months to September.
During the same period last year, Cebu Pacific was cruising on smooth skies with a P9.46-billion profit, showing how drastic the impact of elevated jet fuel prices is.
Cebu Pacific booked a 10-percent growth in revenue to P96.23 billion. However, the airline took a 24-percent hike in expenses to P99.23 billion, as jet fuel rates ballooned to fresh highs.
The airline owned by the Gokongweis earned more revenues as it flew more passengers between January and September. Cebu Pacific’s passenger volume grew by four percent to 20.77 million, showing the resilience of Philippine air travel demand.
This is why Cebu Pacific president and chief commercial officer Alexander Lao is confident the carrier would set a new record for passenger traffic this year in spite of economic risks.
Lao said the airline is projected to surpass the 27-million level in 2026, beating the previous high of 26.88 million last year.
However, Cebu Pacific is suffering from rising prices, recording a 52-percent hike in flying costs to P44.13 billion, as jet fuel prices go up because of security tensions in the Middle East.
The carrier also raised servicing costs by eight percent to P12.41 billion. Cebu Pacific said it has paid more for aircraft servicing due to new fees applied by airport operators.
Still, Cebu Pacific is matching demand with capacity. It will secure a final delivery for an Airbus A330neo by December, leading the industry with a fleet of 100 aircraft.
For 2027, Lao said Cebu Pacific would receive seven new aircraft—all of which are single-aisle jets—as the airline expands its fleet to meet future demand.
Cebu Pacific is the country’s largest carrier by fleet and passenger size, offering more than 2,190 flights weekly to domestic and international destinations.

gem.title: Who benefits from the proposed P350K income tax exemption?
gem.summary: IN his fifth State of the Nation Address on July 27, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. proposed raising the annual personal income tax exemption threshold from P250,000 to P350,000. For workers with taxable income just below the proposed cutoff, the change would wipe out their income tax bill.House Speaker Faustino Dy and Majority Leader Sandro Marcos filed House Bill 10345 to amend the Tax Code. Th…
reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Explains proposed P350K income tax exemption beneficiaries

article.text:
IN his fifth State of the Nation Address on July 27, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. proposed raising the annual personal income tax exemption threshold from P250,000 to P350,000. For workers with taxable income just below the proposed cutoff, the change would wipe out their income tax bill.
House Speaker Faustino Dy and Majority Leader Sandro Marcos filed House Bill 10345 to amend the Tax Code. The bill’s explanatory note says the measure would ease the burden on low- and middle-income earners and help households cope with rising prices.
Workers with annual taxable income above P250,000 and up to P350,000 would no longer owe personal income tax. Those already at or below P250,000 would see no change in their income tax liability.
At P350,000 in annual taxable income, the proposed change would save a worker about P15,000 a year, or the equivalent of P1,250 a month. Those earning above the new threshold would also benefit, with their savings depending on the final rate schedule.
How would the government offset the revenue loss?
The Department of Finance’s proposed Promoting Growth, Revenue and Equity toward Socio-Economic Sustainability Bill pairs targeted tax relief with new or higher levies. The department has proposed higher excise taxes on sweetened beverages, alcohol, vape products and other tobacco-related products. It is also looking at changes to taxes on certain plastic products and other nonessential goods.
The package would raise excise taxes on vehicles valued above P8 million and extend excise taxes to private aircraft and vessels. These measures would shift some of the tax burden from wages to luxury spending.
On the corporate side, the package would exempt micro and small enterprises from the minimum corporate income tax and apply a 15-percent global minimum tax to covered multinational enterprises.
Keeping tax relief in step with inflation
A higher threshold would give workers immediate relief, but inflation would gradually erode its value. Workers who get a raise that merely keeps pace with rising prices could still end up paying a larger share of their income in tax if the brackets stay fixed.
Congress should consider adjusting the threshold and tax brackets automatically for inflation. That would help preserve the value of the relief and spare workers from waiting years for another amendment to the Tax Code. Lawmakers would also have to weigh the cost of those adjustments against the revenue needed to fund public services.
House Bill 10345 was referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means on July 29. As Congress considers the measure, it has two decisions to make: How much relief workers should get now, and how to keep that relief from losing value as prices rise.
Mark S. Gorriceta is the chairman and managing partner of the law firm Gorriceta Africa Cauton & Saavedra (www.gorricetalaw.com).
Gerard Ceasar S. Baguio is a managing associate at Gorriceta Africa Cauton and Saavedra, who specializes in taxation, litigation and real estate.
The firm is a member of the Financial Executives Institute of the Philippines (Finex).

quickHits.title: Metro Manila wholesale construction materials price growth in October hits three-year high
quickHits.summary: WHOLESALE price growth of construction materials in Metro Manila accelerated in October to its strongest reading in more…
reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Construction material prices at three-year high

article.text:
WHOLESALE price growth of construction materials in Metro Manila accelerated in October to its strongest reading in more than three years, driven mainly by higher increases in structural steel prices, while retail price growth remained steady, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said.
The construction materials wholesale price index (CMWPI) in the National Capital Region (NCR) rose 3.7% year on year in October, faster than the 3.4% increase in September, reversing the year-earlier 0.2% decline, according to the PSA.
The October reading was the strongest since the 5.6% recorded in August 2023.
Meanwhile, the construction materials retail price index (CMRPI) rose 2% year on year in October, unchanged for a third consecutive month but exceeding the year-earlier 0.9% increase, the PSA said in a separate report.
The July retail price growth reading of 2.1% had been the strongest since May 2023, when the rate hit 2.6%.
The PSA attributed the acceleration in wholesale price growth mainly to structural steel, which posted a 5.2% increase in October, accelerating from 3% in September.
Wholesale price increases also accelerated for fuels and lubricants (9.7% from 8.9%), sand and gravel (5.5% from 5%), and concrete products (4.9% from 4.8%).
Cement price growth picked up to 3.2% from 2.5% previously, while hardware prices rose 0.9%, against 0.6% increase in September.

article.text:
The National Food Authority (NFA) said on Thursday that farmers may earn up to P8 per kilo after it recently raised the palay buying price to P30 per kilogram.
"Malaking epekto ito sa mga magsasaka. Unang-una, tumaas ang presyo, meaning malaki ang take-home nila. Sa tinatayang P16-P17 production cost eh kung susumahin nga baka kumita sila 'pag pinatuyo nila lahat and all, kumita sila diyan ng mga 7 hanggang P8 per kilo," said NFA administrator Larry Lacson in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.
(This is a big impact for the farmers. First, the price increased, meaning their take-home [pay] is higher. With the estimated P16-P17 production cost, if you sum it all up, they might earn, if they dry everything and all, they could earn around P7 to P8 per kilo.)
The NFA earlier set the buying price for clean and dry palay at P28 to P30 per kilo. Meanwhile, farmers can now also procure 500 bags per cropping season from individual growers, up from the previous ceiling of 200 bags per farmer.

The Philippines,[g] officially the Republic of the Philippines,[h] is an archipelagic country in Southeast Asia. Located in the western Pacific Ocean, it consists of about 7,641 islands, with a total area of about 300,000 square kilometers. The islands are broadly categorized into three main geographical divisions: from north to south, Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. With a population of over 114 million, it is the world's thirteenth-most-populous country.
The Philippines is bounded by the South China Sea to the west, the Philippine Sea to the east, and the Celebes Sea to the south. It shares maritime borders with Taiwan to the north, Japan to the northeast, Palau to southeast, Indonesia to the south, Malaysia to the southwest, Vietnam to the west, and China to the northwest. It has diverse ethnicities and a rich culture. Manila is the country's capital, and its most populated city is Quezon City. Both are within Metro Manila.
Negritos, the archipelago's earliest inhabitants, were followed by waves of Austronesian peoples. The adoption of animism, Hinduism with Buddhist influence, and Islam established island-kingdoms. Extensive overseas trade with neighbors such as the late Tang or Song empire brought Chinese people to the archipelago as well, who would also gradually settle in and intermix over the centuries. Sixteen years ago this Sunday, soldiers slew botanist Leonard Co. He was researching native trees in the mountain forests of Kananga, Leyte when an Army patrol fired at him and four companions. Leonard and two of the four fell dead.
The soldiers initially reported that they ambushed Leonard’s group whom they suspected to be communist rebels. Ambushed! Leonard and the four were unarmed and in civvies. Meaning, the soldiers had lain in wait not at uniformed enemies but at civilians – a clear violation of human rights.
They wasted a genius. Leonard at the time was the country’s foremost botanist. He not only had discovered and co-studied several plant species, among those the Rafflesia aurantia, Rafflesia leonardi, Xanthostemon fruticosus, and Vaccinium oscarlopezianum. He also trained dozens of botanists, naming and describing to them from memory more than 10,000 indigenous flora.

I have been laid low by the infernal flu/cough virus and I swear that as I carry on in years, the bouts and the recovery have been long and draining, almost depressing.
I now fear future possibilities where you literally go two to three nights without sleep due to the sound and feeling of drowning, so much so that we have opened our eyes to finding a used Lazy Boy chair to sleep in upright!
I have also been captured if not enchanted by AI movies that take off from “The Hobbit” and the “Lord of the Rings.” I warn you all before curiosity gets you, it is beyond habit forming that my own daughter calls it my recuperation with addiction binge watching!
Watching warlocks and war dogs has had me thinking of replacing our sweet old Great Dane Missy, while my wife Karen wants to adopt a retired K9 to reward it with a spoiled life.
I don’t know if it’s a sign, but I received an email about K9…
